text.p: British drugs discovery company Chiroscience Group Plc and Darwin Molecular Corp said their proposed merger was a perfect match, uniting the chemical expertise of Chiroscience with Darwin's biology know-how.
"Chiroscience is a very strong chemistry company -- we wanted to get more access to underlying biology," Chiroscience chief executive John Padfield told Reuters.

David Galas, Darwin's chief scientific officer, said Darwin needed a link up to move on to translating early stage research based on gene discovery into products. "The synergy and match is perfect for this...it is a match made in heaven," he said.

Under the deal, Chiroscience will issue shares to shareholders in the privately-owned Darwin, based on a value of $120 million. The stock market greeted the deal, with Chiroscience shares gaining 11-1/2p to 360 after touching 375p.
Chiroscience said the merger would give it access to further novel drug discovery programmes from genomics, which Galas said in future would give understanding of the fundamental disease mechanism.
"Accelerating the drug discovery process is very important -- it is very competitive and very costly," Padfield said.
"More skills in your toolbox means you are going to get that crucial material into testing that much faster.

Chiroscience had already collaborated at a research level with Darwin, and Padfield said Darwin's gene technology would help it in its work on drugs for cancer and arthritis based on MMP inhibitors, which aim to stop cells from spreading.
"It will help our MMP programme -- we'll be able to get those drugs more selectively designed in the medium term," Padfield said.
Chiroscience aims to have its Levobupivacaine anaesthetic in some markets in 1998, which Padfield said would be the immediate driver for the company's move towards profitability.
"But long-term profitability will come from extensive drug discovery, he said, adding that with "a good wind", and Darwin's help, that would come.

Both companies wish to retain their staff, and the deal is cemented by Galas joining the Chiroscience board as an executive director. Darwin chairman Ronald Cape will join Chiroscience as a non-executive director, and Darwin's Leroy Hood will chair the combined company's scientific advisory board.
